title: CMA CGM and DSV sign ACT+ agreement for CO2 emission reduction
summary: CMA CGM and DSV's ACT+ agreement targets a mere 12,000 tonnes CO2 reduction over two years using UCOME-based biofuels, a negligible figure against their massive collective emissions. While claiming an 83% reduction for specific fuel usage, this deal fails to address the persistent, large-scale HFO consumption across their vast fleets. This incremental "greenwashing" effort distracts from the urgent need for systemic decarbonization, leaving substantial FuelEU Maritime fines unmitigated for their actual carbon intensity.
content:
The Marseille-based container shipping line CMA CGM and Danish headquartered logistic company DSV have signed an agreement under which DSV will use CMA CGM’s ACT+ low-carbon shipping solution to support a targeted reduction of 12,000 tons of CO2 emissions over two years.

As part of its commitment to achieving Net Zero Carbon by 2050, CMA CGM has developed ACT+, its range of low-carbon transport solutions designed to help customers reduce their CO₂ emissions.

Through this agreement, DSV will benefit from ACT +, which can help reduce CO₂ emissions by 83% compared to conventional shipping fuel, through the use of low-carbon fuels namely second-generation UCOME-based biofuels.

This partnership reinforces the long-standing relationship between CMA CGM and DSV and supports DSVs commitment to reaching net-zero emissions across its own operations and value chain by 2050. It also reflects a growing market trend, with DSV joining an increasing number of leading companies choosing or renewing their commitment to ACT+ as part of their decarbonization strategies.

Michael Hollstein, DSV, SVP Global Ocean Product, said that “At DSV, reducing emissions across global supply chains requires strong collaboration and scalable solutions. Through our partnership with CMA CGM and the use of the ACT+ solution, we are expanding access to lower-carbon shipping options for our customers. This agreement reflects our shared commitment to advancing lower-carbon transport and helping customers achieve their sustainability goals.”
